items.q: The city where our Beloved Prophet ﷺ was born.
The year of his birth is known by this name.
The month of his birth, by the most famous view.
The father of our Beloved Master ﷺ, who died before He ﷺ was born.
The mother of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The wet-nurse of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ in the desert.
The grandfather who cared for him after his mother died.
The uncle who raised and protected him.
The title the people of Makkah gave him for his honesty.
Our Beloved Master's ﷺ first wife, a noble merchant woman.
items.a: Our lady Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا)

items.q: The age at which the first revelation came.
The first man (adult free man) to accept Islam.
items.a: Our master Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The first child to accept Islam.
items.a: Our master 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The first woman to accept Islam.
The tribe of our Beloved Master ﷺ.
Our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ clan within Quraysh.
The first muezzin, who was tortured for his faith in Makkah.
The night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem.
The ascent through the heavens.
The migration to Madinah.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ was born in this year, by the common estimate.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ was this age when His ﷺ mother died.
The place where his mother died, on the way back from Madinah.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ was this age when His ﷺ grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib died.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ worked as a young man looking after these.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ was this age when He ﷺ married our lady Khadijah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا).
The servant of Khadijah who travelled with him on her trade to al-Sham.
The Christian scholar, cousin of Khadijah, who said the revelation was the same as came to Musa (paraphrased).
After a pause in revelation, our Beloved Master ﷺ said "Wrap me up" (meaning), and this surah came down.
For about this many years, the call to Islam was private.
The hill from which he called Quraysh openly.
The house in Makkah where early Muslims met in secret.
The first martyr in Islam, the mother of 'Ammar.
The country the first Muslims migrated to.
The just Christian king of Abyssinia who protected them.
The Companion who spoke for the Muslims before al-Najashi.
items.a: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The surah Ja'far (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) recited to al-Najashi.
The boycott of Banu Hashim lasted about this many years.
The valley where Banu Hashim were besieged.
The "Year of Sorrow" was when these two died.
items.a: Our lady Khadijah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا) and Abu Talib

items.q: The town our Beloved Prophet ﷺ visited to call its people, where He ﷺ was stoned.
The Christian boy from Nineveh who offered him grapes at Ta'if.
The animal he rode on the Isra'.
On the Mi'raj, the prayers were reduced from fifty to this many.
The Prophet who advised him on the Mi'raj to ask for fewer prayers.
The Companion who believed the Isra' at once and got the title "al-Siddiq".
items.a: Our master Abu Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The first pledge at 'Aqabah was made by this many people of Yathrib.
The Companion sent to teach the people of Yathrib after the first pledge.
The second pledge of 'Aqabah was made by about this many men and two women.
The two tribes of Yathrib.
The house where Quraysh met to plot against our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The Companion who slept in our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ bed on the night of the Hijrah.
items.a: Our master 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The cave where our Beloved Master ﷺ and our master Abu Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) hid for three nights.
The verse "Do not grieve; Allah is with us" (meaning) is in this surah.
The daughter of Abu Bakr called "Dhat al-Nitaqayn".
items.a: Asma' bint Abi Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا)

items.q: The guide they hired for the Hijrah journey.
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (named in Sirat Ibn Hisham)

items.q: The rider who chased them and whose horse sank into the sand.
The first mosque built in Islam.
The Hijrah took place in this CE year.
The Companion who freed Bilal (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) by buying him.
items.a: Our master Abu Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The master who tortured Bilal (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) on the hot sand.
The word Bilal (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) repeated under torture.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ prayed that Islam be strengthened by one of two men: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab or this man.
Our master 'Umar (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) accepted Islam after hearing this surah at his sister's house.
The uncle of our Beloved Master ﷺ who accepted Islam shortly before 'Umar and was called "Lion of Allah".
items.a: Our master Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The Quraysh leader who said the Qur'an was magic after admitting its beauty, and about whom Surah al-Muddaththir speaks.
The Quraysh envoy sent to bring the Muslims back from Abyssinia, who later became a Companion.
The emigration to Abyssinia happened in this year of prophethood.
The boycott document was eaten by this, except the name of Allah.
The man of Ta'if's journey who offered protection when our Beloved Prophet ﷺ returned to Makkah.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ was offered that the angel of the mountains crush the people of Ta'if; He ﷺ hoped for this instead.
items.a: That their descendants would worship Allah

items.q: Our Beloved Master ﷺ led the Blessed Prophets (عليهم السلام) in prayer on the Isra' at this mosque.
On the Mi'raj, he was offered milk and wine and chose this.
The first pledge of 'Aqabah is also called this, as it had no pledge to fight.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ arrived at Quba' on this day of the week, by the common view.
The son of Abu Bakr who brought them news in the cave each night.
The freedman of Abu Bakr who grazed sheep to hide their tracks.
The reward Quraysh offered for capturing our Beloved Master ﷺ and Abu Bakr.
The scholar who wrote al-Sirah, the earliest major biography, later edited by Ibn Hisham.
The Andalusian commentary on Ibn Hisham's Sirah by al-Suhayli رحمة الله عليه.
The book of Qadi 'Iyad رحمة الله عليه on our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ rights and qualities.
The Seerah of al-Halabi رحمة الله عليه, widely read in Ottoman lands.
The book of al-Qastallani رحمة الله عليه on the Seerah and our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ virtues.
The Christian monk of Busra who recognised signs of prophethood in the boy Muhammad ﷺ.
The pact of chivalry in Makkah to defend the wronged, which our Beloved Prophet ﷺ attended.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ settled a dispute over placing this stone when the Ka'bah was rebuilt.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ settled the Black Stone dispute by putting the stone on this, so every clan could lift it.
The age of our Beloved Master ﷺ when Quraysh rebuilt the Ka'bah.
The opening of the chest (shaqq al-sadr) first happened while he was with this nurse.
The first Muslim to recite the Qur'an aloud publicly in Makkah, according to Ibn Ishaq.
The tribe from al-Madinah whose six men met our Beloved Prophet ﷺ at 'Aqabah the year before the first pledge.
The number of leaders (nuqaba') chosen at the second pledge.
The Jewish rabbi of Madinah who accepted Islam soon after the Hijrah.
The Companion with whom our Beloved Prophet ﷺ first stayed in Madinah.
Our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ camel, which chose where He ﷺ would stay.
The caliph who made the Hijrah the start of the Islamic calendar.
items.a: Our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The woman whose dry goat gave milk when our Beloved Prophet ﷺ passed her tent.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ left Makkah on the Hijrah in this month.
Ibn Hisham رحمة الله عليه died in this year.
items.src: Wafayat al-A'yan (Ibn Khallikan); to be checked

items.q: The Ansari Companion who led the second pledge, among the twelve leaders (nuqaba').
items.src: Sirat Ibn Hisham; to be checked
